Today's updates include news on the November cyclone for the Chennai–Puducherry coast.

## November cyclone for the Chennai–Puducherry coast
Cyclone Akvan, which was previously a severe cyclonic storm, has now significantly weakened. It made landfall on November twentieth at Ganjam district as a weakened cyclonic storm and rapidly degraded into a low-pressure area the same day. Its land interaction commenced along the Andhra-Odisha coast, and it has since dissipated as a tropical depression. Following this, the Odisha government is beginning damage assessment from November twenty-second.

Despite Cyclone Akvan's dissipation, the Regional Meteorological Centre in Chennai has issued a yellow alert for Chennai and twenty other districts in Tamil Nadu. This alert forecasts heavy rainfall on November twenty-fourth, with twenty-one districts in total expected to be affected. The heavy rain is anticipated in Chennai, Tiruvallur, Chengalpattu, and other northern, delta, and southern districts. The forecast indicates a seventy-five percent chance of rain for Chennai on November twenty-fourth. This weather activity is expected to continue with thunderstorms and lightning in isolated places across Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, and Karaikal between November twenty-third and twenty-sixth.
